rules_text:
Rules summary Overview Ensure one of the factions you support wins whilst providing the best support for that faction Turn On your turn, first play a card from your hand and activate its effect OR discard up to 3 cards facedown into the Wilderness After which, draw back up to 4 cards from either the faceup Tavern or the facedown Harbour deck After which, discard down to 3 cards facedown to the Wilderness Some Heroes are played hidden, and these may be later revealed but their actions won't be triggered, hidden heroes do NOT count towards end game trigger but do count for scoring Game End The game ends when a player has a certain number of visible heroes based on the player count (5-8) 2 players - 8 heroes 3 players - 7 heroes 4 players - 7 heroes 5 players - 6 heroes 6 players - 5 heroes After which, first determine the winning faction Undead win if red & green are both in the dark spaces, if this causes a tie with the other win conditions Undead win Water Folk win if red & green are in the same space or on adjacent spaces Empire wins if red is at least 2 spaces ahead of green Tribes win if green is at least 2 spaces ahead of red If your secret leader matches the winning team, you MAY win If you are the ONLY player with a matching leader, you win! If multiple players match, the player with the most heroes of the winning faction wins! If tied, the player with the lowest total heroes wins! If still tied, the leader with the highest card number wins!

---

The island of Oshra is in turmoil. Following the death of the Emperor, the conflict between the Hill Tribes and the Imperial Army escalated. While the Water People try to maintain balance between the old rivals, the Undead aim to escalate the war. All hope rests on the six children of the Emperor: Who of them will claim the throne?

In Hidden Leaders, you take the role of one of six secret leaders, each of them is allied with two of the four factions/colors. By playing heroes into your tableau, either openly or secretly, you influence the outcome of the conflict.

At the end of the game, one of the four factions will win:

     Red leading > Red victory
     Green leading > Green victory
     Tie between Red & Green > Blue victory
     Red & Green in War Zone > Black victory


Each player who is aligned with the winning faction can claim the victory. However, they must have more heroes of this color than any competitor.

Hidden Leaders is a quick, light strategy card game with direct player interaction. It combines tableau building and deduction elements with its unique winning mechanism. This is a game of great tension with no-down time, that’s fast to learn. Its distinctive artwork and character names will make you smile.

—description from designer
community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] Delivery of the game for US buyers delayed until at least mid-May 2022 while the game is already on the US soil while you charged us $9 for delivery and your KS campaign advertised a January 2022 delivery is totally unacceptable. Worst part is that you didn’t even apologize about it. First and last time I will make a pledge for your kickstarters.

[Rating: 1/10] Game does not really work. What you do on your turn isn't interesting and the overall idea of figuring out what faction people are on is meaningless. The game state is so out of your control it doesn't matter if you figure out what someone is trying to do.

[Rating: 1/10] Hidden Leaders has a cool concept, but it's often too chaotic and opaque — it’s hard to strategize when hidden goals clash randomly. Player influence feels diluted, especially with more players

[Rating: 2/10] This is not my kind of game - very tight competitive game where you should really be trying to kick the right opponent at the right time to leap frog forward, and yet fridgin high luck of the draw. It doesn't matter to me how short it is - it is as much time I am spending not enjoying myself once I've understood what the game is about.

[Rating: 2/10] Terrible game. What you're doing throughout the whole game is moving two markers up and down a ladder. Whatever limited variety there exists on the cards is not particularly interesting given that all you're doing is the above trotting back and forth of markers. What one player does (move marker 1-3 spots) is often undone by another and so on.  Very limited interesting choices - even for a short game this is an absolute bore and has been viewed as such by the groups I've tried it with.   Nice art though!

[Rating: 2/10] Too complex for that kind of game. You would like to be able to put this on a table with new players as a party game, but there is a steep learning curve (iconography, leaders' victory conditions, possible cards power, etc.) which prevents this. Also the game is difficult to read while playing when you play with an high number of player as you are supposed to read the text of the cards put in front of the other players across the table. [Rating: 2.6/10] at 5+ competent  players, whoever acts last just wins.  facedown  cards should count  for your faction  count. you should be able  to  play  hidden cards as your turn.

[Rating: 3/10] I wanted to like this because I LOVE the art, but the the game has three flaws in the core game-play that ruin it for me 1) the last play decides the winning faction, which means everything else that happened in the game doesn't matter much, 2) there is little hidden information, since the it is easy to know factions midway through, and 3) the factions are at odds, meaning you are really only ever going for one faction. There is some sort of fun game here somewhere, but it just doesn't shine through.

[Rating: 3/10] Stunning artwork but it's not enough to carry the mediocre and frankly pretty boring tug-of-war gameplay. Gave this game three chances to win me over since I really wanted to like it, but my group never found any of the decisions that interesting and the deduction was super lackluster.

[Rating: 3/10] I'm sadly not impressed by Hidden Leaders. I think the people behind it are awesome and that's what @Kickstarter is about, and that the artwork by @hiziri_pro is outstanding (it's a shame that the cardstock doesn't do it justice and it fades).?
